facts_read.architecture: the map is a background view that persists for the app's lifetime, mediated by three components: a Layer Manager, a Padding Provider and a Camera Director
facts_read.layer_manager: each feature creates its own map layer and registers it; the layer's interface exposes add/remove for markers, polygons, polylines and tile overlays but no access to other layers; an 'exclusive' layer temporarily hides all others; every layer must be bound to a RIBs Interactor so it dies with the feature
facts_read.padding_provider: chrome registers itself as a padding source; the provider aggregates edge insets into an observable stream so region-fitting code knows the visible map area
facts_read.camera_director: features register camera rules listing coordinates that must be visible; the director aggregates them, and one feature at a time may request exclusive camera control
facts_read.public_interfaces: MapLayerManager.add(layer, interactorScope, exclusive) / remove(layer); MapLayer.add|remove(marker|polygon|polyline|tileOverlay); MapPaddingProvider.edgeInsetsStream + add/remove(paddingSource, viewControllerScope); MapCameraDirector.add/remove(cameraRule) + requestCameraControl/relinquishCameraControl

sources.corroborates: the artifact's own structure, independently and in the vendor's words: 488 `MapLayer` implementations that attach layers per feature, padding-inset handling on the map view, camera-listener plumbing, an active-map counter, and tile-overlay support — the same four ideas the post names
